sections.label: Construction support and wage subsidies
sections.summary: Measures introduced include a $1.36 billion Construction Support Package, Foreign Worker Levy waivers and rebates, and Jobs Support Scheme wage subsidies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Amongst other measures, we introduced a $1.36 billion Construction Support Package, extended waivers and rebates of the Foreign Worker Levy, and provided wage subsidies under the Jobs Support Scheme.

sections.label: Universal extension for construction contracts
sections.summary: Part 8A legislated a universal extension of time of four months, or 122 days, for construction contracts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Under Part 8A, we legislated for a universal extension of time of four months, or 122 days, for construction contracts.

sections.label: BCA projects awarded this year
sections.summary: The Building Control Authority estimates that $23 billion to $28 billion worth of projects will be awarded this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: The Building Control Authority (BCA) estimates that $23 billion to $28 billion worth of projects will be awarded this year.

sections.label: Extension for construction and supply contracts
sections.summary: Temporary relief measures for construction and supply contracts are intended to be extended six months, to 30 September 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: First, for construction and supply contracts, we intend to extend the temporary relief measures for a period of six months, to 30 September 2021.

sections.label: Extending cost-sharing relief under Part 8B
sections.summary: In consultation with industry partners, the cost-sharing relief under Part 8B is intended to be extended another six months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: This ripple effect could result in further construction delays or uncompleted projects.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Therefore, in consultation with industry partners, we believe that it is prudent to extend this cost-sharing relief under Part 8B for another six months.

sections.label: Extension for property purchase agreements
sections.summary: Temporary relief measures under Part 2 for options to purchase and sale and purchase agreements are intended to be extended three months, to 30 June 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: For options to purchase and agreements for the sale and purchase of residential, commercial and industrial properties with developers, including those with HDB, we intend to extend the temporary relief measures under Part 2 for a further period of three months, to 30 June 2021.

sections.label: Extending sunset period one year
sections.summary: The proposal is to extend the sunset period by another year, until 19 April 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Specifically, we propose to extend the sunset period for another year, until 19 April 2022.

sections.label: Part 8C delivery extension
sections.summary: Part 8C will let developers who cannot reach an arrangement extend delivery of possession up to the four-month, or 122-day, universal extension for construction projects.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: For developers who are unable to come to an arrangement and require help, Part 8C will then allow them to extend the date of delivery of possession up to the universal extension of time provided for construction projects which is four months, or 122 days.

sections.label: Bill supports construction sector
sections.summary: The Bill is part of Government efforts to partner the industry so the ecosystem functions, construction progresses and industrial capabilities are kept.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: While the sector has been severely impacted with the onset of COVID-19, it has shown great resilience to get back on its feet.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: The Government is committed to partner the industry to ensure that the ecosystem continues to function, construction work continues to progress smoothly and we do not lose important industrial capabilities, even as we transform the sector.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: This Bill is an important part of this effort to ensure the sector stays on its feet and emerge stronger.

sections.label: Arresting manpower cost surge
sections.summary: Beyond this Bill, it is necessary to arrest the manpower cost surge that has dramatically increased construction costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Beyond this Bill, it is necessary to arrest the manpower cost surge which has led to a dramatic increase in construction costs.

sections.label: High migrant worker quarantine cost
sections.summary: The industry faces a quarantine cost of $2,400 per migrant worker, which has not decreased despite moving quarantine to dedicated non-hotel facilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: The industry faces high quarantine cost of $2,400 per migrant worker, which has not decreased even as we move quarantine from hotels to dedicated non-hotel facilities.

sections.label: Forward deploying resources in Asia
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Government can work with the Built Environment sector to forward deploy resources in key cities in India and Bangladesh.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Given that a large number of general construction migrant workers come from countries such as India and Bangladesh, is it possible for the Government to work with the Built Environment sector to forward deploy resources in key cities in these countries, given that COVID-19 vaccination is proceeding very slowly in Asia.

sections.label: Extension for Built Environment sector
sections.summary: An extension of the temporary measures is needed to give the Built Environment sector more time for a soft landing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: An extension of the temporary measures today is very much needed to give the Built Environment sector more time to achieve a soft landing.

sections.label: Clause 2 extends Act validity
sections.summary: Clause 2 extends the validity of Parts 1 and 2 of the Act for another year to 19 April next year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Clause 2 extends the validity of Parts 1 and 2 of the Act for another year to 19 April next year.

sections.label: Part 3 bankruptcy thresholds ending
sections.summary: Part 3 raised bankruptcy and winding up thresholds and payment periods, and this Bill confirms Part 3 ends on 19 April this year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To recap, Part 3 had among other things, raised the threshold for individual bankruptcy and corporate winding up from a debt of $15,000, to $60,000 and $100,000 respectively.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It had also increased the time period to pay from three weeks from demand to six months.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This Bill confirms that the provisions of Part 3 will end on 19 April this year as scheduled.

sections.label: Explaining no Part 3 extension
sections.summary: The Government should explain why it decided there was no need to extend Part 3 to give breathing space from insolvency proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On this note, it will be most useful for the Government to explain why it decided that there was no need to extend Part 3 of the Act to give individuals and businesses continued breathing space from insolvency proceedings.

sections.label: Clarify factors for extensions
sections.summary: The Minister is asked to clarify what factors were considered before granting the initial four-month and now six-month extensions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can Minister clarify what factors were considered before granting the initial four-month extension in November and now this six-month extension?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: One year after the start of the pandemic, we are granting a second extension of contract deadlines that is even longer than the first extension.

sections.label: Temporary scheme to rehire workers
sections.summary: The construction industry needs workers, so MND is urged to create a temporary scheme to rehire repatriated Work Permit and S Pass workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In the short run, our construction industry needs workers to fulfill the projects it has already committed to based on pre-pandemic labour conditions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Therefore, I hope that MND works with other Government Ministries to create a temporary scheme, where employers can more easily rehire Work Permit and S Pass workers who have been repatriated to their countries in the past year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: MND has taken some steps in this direction by allowing workers that have previously obtained the necessary Skills Evaluation Certificate (Knowledge) test (SEC(K) test) qualifications in a particular trade to return and work in the same trade in Singapore, without retaking the test.

sections.label: Developer delivery date extension and assessors
sections.summary: Clause 3 lets developers further extend delivery dates only after a 122-day total extension, and asks about assessors' credentials and independence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Clause 3 of the Bill provides that the developer may only further extend the delivery date after the developer has already extended the original delivery date by a total of 122 days.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: As for the assessors appointed by the Government, would the Ministry provide details about them, such as their backgrounds and professional credentials and how does the Ministry determine that they are independent?

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Since the developers are allowed under the law to delay the projects, these developers should not file claims and lawsuits against sub-contractors downstream.

sections.label: Construction workforce and Bill support
sections.summary: As of December 2020 about 116,300 Singaporeans and 288,700 foreigners worked in construction, and the Bill extends interim relief measures six months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: According to the Labour Market Report, as of December 2020, there were about 116,300 Singaporeans and 288,700 foreigners working in the construction industry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding my queries above, I support this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This Bill extends many of the interim relief measures that were provided to the construction sector to deal with COVID-19 for a further six months.

sections.label: Purchaser claims for rental expenses
sections.summary: Provisions let purchasers claim a portion of additional rental expenses from developers during delay, and ask for data on usage and financial impact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: To cushion the blow for these purchasers, there are provisions here permitting them to make claims against the developers for a portion of any additional rental expenses they may incur as a result of having to find alternative accommodation during the period of delay.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Is the Minister of State able to share any data on how many purchasers have used this provision and what is the overall financial impact of these payments on developers would be?

sections.label: Reasonable payments down value chain
sections.summary: Suggests developers and main contractors pay lower-tier contractors for partial completion even if entire milestones are not completed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: My suggestion to deal with this would be for developers and main contractors in turn to take a more reasonable approach in making payments to contractors lower down the value chain for partial completion of work, even if this means entire milestones may not have been completed as required under the contract.

sections.label: Relief notifications and assessor determinations
sections.summary: About 1,100 relief notifications were filed as of 19 March 2021, and only about 118, or 10%, applied for an assessor's determination.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: For construction and supply contracts, there have been about 1,100 notifications for relief filed as of 19 March 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Of those, only about 118, or about 10%, eventually applied for an assessor’s determination.

sections.label: Part 3 sunset and insolvency lapse
sections.summary: Part 3's sunset period ends 19 April 2021, but its insolvency measures already lapsed in October 2020, prescribed period 20 April to 19 October 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: To clarify to the Member, while the sunset period for Part 3 ends on 19 April 2021, nonetheless, the measures relating to insolvency in Part 3 had already lapsed in October 2020 as the prescribed period was from 20 April 2020 to 19 October 2020.

sections.label: Advance payments for public sector projects
sections.summary: At least $665 million of advance payment in total has been provided for public sector projects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: For public sector projects, we have provided at least $665 million of advance payment in total.

sections.label: COVID-19 construction delay relief extension
sections.summary: Under Part 8C, developers facing COVID-19 construction delays may serve notice for a delivery date extension of up to four months, or 122 days.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Under Part 8C, developers who face construction delays due to COVID-19 and require relief may serve a notice for an extension of the delivery date by up to four months, or 122 days, which is aligned with the period in Part 8A.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: This was also shared during the Second Reading of the COTMA Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: It is because construction work stopped for approximately two months due to the circuit breaker period, and works were further delayed by at least another two months as all dormitories were only cleared in early August 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Therefore, adding two months together, two plus two, that is four months and 122 days.

sections.label: Relief for affected property agreements
sections.summary: The relief applies to all affected housing, commercial and industrial property sale and purchase agreements meeting the Act's criteria, regardless of when Part 8C operates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Ms Lim will be pleased to know that the relief will apply to all affected agreements for the sale and purchase of housing, commercial and industrial property that meet the criteria stated in the Act, regardless of when Part 8C comes into operation.

sections.label: Assessor role and no lawyer representation
sections.summary: The assessor makes just and fair decisions and may request information from both parties, while companies cannot be represented by lawyers in assessments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: The overarching role of the assessor is to make a decision that is just and fair in the circumstances and they have the power to ask for the appropriate information and documents from both parties, including information or documents not sought for by either party to achieve this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: In the first instance, we hope to minimise the need for developers and purchases to even require an assessor's determination and we will lay out clearly the qualifying costs that purchasers will be able to seek reimbursement for to make the process more efficient and easy for everyone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: The Member will also know that in the ordinary case, if the matter were to go to Court, the company would have a right to legal representation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Therefore, we have taken the position that for assessments, companies cannot be represented by lawyers.
